headline: Approved past meeting minutes and kept 2027 regular meetings on the second Wednesday of each month.
summary: Commissioners discussed a food waste fee schedule at the transfer station, which the council must approve. They also talked about a possible textile swap series at the Rectory Barn and a state tire program. Recruiting new members and a central theme for Earth Day 2027 were also discussed.
decisions: Approved previous meeting minutes unanimously, with minor edits to the spelling of names.
Voted unanimously to keep regular meetings for 2027 on the second Wednesday of the month at 7 PM.

TOWN OF HAMDEN, CONNECTICUT 
 
Solid Waste & Recycling Commission 
Minutes         
         
Regular Meeting 
 
7:00 PM, November 11, 2026 
 
 
 
Hamden Government 
Center 
2750 Dixwell Avenue 
Hamden, CT  06518 
Tel:  (203) 287-7070 
Fax:  (203) 287-7075 
 Click to View Agenda   
  
1. CALL TO ORDER 
  
 
• Chairperson Kosowsky called the meeting to order at 7:06PM 
 
2. ATTENDANCE 
  
 
• In attendance: Alice Kosowsky, Chairperson, Joe DeRisi, Recycling Coordinator, Eben Pariser, 
Commissioner, Shenira Billups, Commissioner, and Commissioner Theresa Allgood. 
 
3. APPROVAL OF PREVIOUS MEETING MINUTES 
  
 
• The Commission approved the minutes unanimously with minor edits on the misspelling of 
names.    
 
4. PUBLIC COMMENT 
  
 
• No Comments.  
 
5. CORRESPONDENCE 
There will be a brief summary of the correspondence submitted between the last 
correspondence update and this one. This includes but is not limited to any 
correspondence with council members that members wish to submit for the record. It can 
also include written communication to the council from the administration, community 
members, etc.   
 
• No Corresponence.
6. EXECUTIVE SESSION 
(if recommended by the town attorney)  
 
• Not needed. 
 
7. REPORTS 
  
 
• The Chairperson attended a grant workshop from the World Wildlife Fund, which, together with 
the Institute for Local Self-Reliance, are putting up grants ranging from $75,000 to $250,000 to 
support social media outreach for residential food waste composting. A program is needed in 
order to apply for this funding. Remains to be seen if our anaerobic digester counts can qualify 
(check if SCROG is on it). 
• Spring Glen School is interested in replicating the Bear Path recycling program. Joe suggested 
DeRisi is coordinating this. 
 
8. OLD BUSINESS 
  
 
 
  1. Food Waste Composting at the Transfer Station. Joe DeRisi, Recycling Coordinator, 
to report on regional and local events.  
  
• Currently, no new information on the research from the National Lab of the Rockies, but 
Joe will update the commission as soon as new information comes in. 
• Commissioners are reviewing a fee schedule related to food waste at the transfer station. 
This will take time because the change has to be approved by the council, but what is clear 
is that we need to simplify the fee schedule.  
• Can we balance our efforts to encourage people to bring food waste to the transfer station 
with the need to charge a fee for this service? 
 
  2. Textile collection. Alice Kosowsky, SW&R Chairperson, to update the Commission 
regarding meeting at the Rectory Barn with Bob Zoni from the Hamden Historical 
Society.  
  
• Chairperson Kosowski and Joe DeRisi met with Bob Zoni, who has provided a plan on the 
restoration of the barn, which could be used to store clothing, but also, potentially serve as 
one of the venues for our textile swaps. 
• The Commission is exploring the potential of holding a textile swap series. 
 
  3. Tire Request for Proposal. Joe DeRisi to update on recent Mayor’s Office decisions.  
  
• Joe has shared a memorandum with Public Works on tires, waiting to see if the town’s 
attorney needs to review it. 
• The importance of signing up for the state's program, which would benefit us to the tune of 
$30K-$40K savings a year. 
• How do we find a good balance between town and state programs to avoid violating any 
existing statute? One foreseeable possibility is that paint, electronics, mattresses, and tires
and any other state-sponsored programs could be looked at outside the gate, and organics 
would be taken all the way to the back of the transfer station. In other words, we have to 
find a way to divert some of it to deal with the issue of mixed loads which often leads to 
confusion, confrontation, and abuse. 
 
  4. Earth Day: brainstorming regarding central theme for 2027, involving other local 
groups.  
  
• What should be the central theme? Food Security, or Sustainability Pays? For food 
security, composting food waste helps to build soils, which are then useful for growing 
food). 
• Work on creating a list of vendors and a QR code to follow that brings people to the 
Hamden Earth Day page. 
 
9. NEW BUSINESS 
  
 
 
  1. New Members, both Youth and Adult.   
  
• More efforts are needed to recruit new members, especially as we seek to communicate 
with the new generation. 
• Acknowledging that effective recruitment will depend on the limitations put on 
Commissioners, such as geographic location, and others, as well as how we communicate 
success stories like our textile swap program. 
• Commissioner Billups to share details with attendees of a CT BIPOC Wellness Initiative 
meeting this week, and the Youth Alliance. 
 
  2. SCRCOG Meeting on 12/9/26, which happens to be SW&R Commission’s scheduled 
regular meeting. Vote on Commissioners’ preferences.  
  
• The Commission unanimously voted to keep its regular meetings for 2027 on the second 
Wednesday of the month at 7PM. 
 
10. ADJOURNMENT 
  
 
• Commissioner Theresa motioned to dismiss the meeting at 8:14 PM. The motion was seconded by 
the Chairperson and approved unanimously.
